diagnosis: The mobile pairing confirmation endpoint verifies that pairing_code exists in Redis, but writes the approval state for desktop_session_id provided in the request body without ensuring that desktop_session_id is the session associated with that specific pairing_code. An attacker can authorize desktop sessions on other devices.
exploit_request:
POST /auth/device-pairing/authorize HTTP/1.1
Host: login.desktopconnect.io
Authorization: Bearer <victim_mobile_token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"pairing_code": "PAIR-9901-4412", "desktop_session_id": "sess_attacker_remote_rig_01"}
corrected_code:
@router.post("/auth/device-pairing/authorize")
async def authorize_desktop_device_pairing(
    pairing_code: str = Body(..., embed=True),
    desktop_session_id: str = Body(..., embed=True),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    redis: Redis = Depends(get_redis_client)
):
    stored_session = await redis.get(f"pairing_code:{pairing_code}")
    if not stored_session or stored_session != desktop_session_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid pairing code or session mismatch")

    await redis.delete(f"pairing_code:{pairing_code}")
    await redis.set(
        f"desktop_auth:{desktop_session_id}",
        json.dumps({"user_id": str(current_user.id), "status": "APPROVED"}),
        ex=300
    )
    return {"status": "pairing_confirmed", "session_id": desktop_session_id}
